title: Two audits of a waterfront lease reached very different answers

beats.text: The Ramp restaurant and San Francisco Boatworks shared a Port tenant.
The lease tied part of the rent to gross receipts.

beats.text: The audit separately identified $185 in unpaid base rent.
The Port said it would invoice the tenant and pursue collection.

visual.kicker: San Francisco Controller, City Services Auditor

beats.text: Years later, the auditors could not match checks to rent bills.

visual.kicker: San Francisco Controller, City Services Auditor

visual.heading: What the later auditors could trace

beats.text: the tenant provided no supporting payment documents.

visual.text: Port Commission: Audit of St. Francis Marine Center for January 1, 2018, Through December 31, 2021, Could Not Be Completed Because of Pending Litigation and Lack of Records
visual.mark: Port Commission: Audit of St. Francis Marine Center for January 1, 2018, Through December 31, 2021, Could Not Be Completed Because of Pending Litigation and Lack of Records

beats.text: Some Port receipts also left out the period or purpose.
Counsel disclosed litigation alleging the tenant’s former controller misrepresented rent payments.

visual.kicker: San Francisco Controller, City Services Auditor

beats.text: The auditors could not determine whether the tenant complied from 2018 through 2021.
In March 2026, the Port said it was negotiating with the tenant.

visual.kicker: San Francisco Controller, City Services Auditor

beats.text: The Controller later listed the audit as closed.

visual.kicker: San Francisco Controller, City Services Auditor

beats.text: That list gives neither a reconstructed rent balance nor a court outcome.
